summary.title: WildDet3D: Scaling Promptable 3D Detection in the Wild

details: Monocular 3D detectors are locked to one prompt interface (text OR oracle 2D box), cannot exploit extra geometric cues when a sensor provides depth, and are trained on datasets covering <100 categories in narrow domains, so they fail in the open world.

WildDet3D: a single geometry-aware promptable detector that natively accepts text, 2D point, 2D box, and visual-exemplar prompts and predicts metric 3D boxes (center, dimensions, SO(3) rotation, confidence) from one RGB image.

Core mechanism: dual encoders — a segmentation-pretrained image encoder for semantics and a separate RGBD/depth encoder whose depth latents are injected into the visual features via a zero-initialized ControlNet-style residual, making depth input strictly optional (zero-filled when absent) so the model degrades gracefully to monocular; a deeply supervised 3D head cross-attends to camera-ray (spherical-harmonic) and depth latents with unambiguous rotation/dimension normalization.

WildDet3D-Data: a 1M-image, 13.5K-category in-the-wild 3D detection dataset built by generating multiple candidate 3D boxes for existing 2D annotations with five complementary lifting methods and keeping only human- or VLM-verified candidates.
Image encoder: SAM 3 ViT-H + SimpleFPN, first 28/32 blocks frozen; input 1008x1008.
RGBD encoder: LingBot-Depth DINOv2 ViT-L/14 at 686x686 with 4-channel RGBD input, last 3/24 blocks trainable; training samples depth as 70% zero (monocular), 20% patch-masked, 10% full.

3D box parameterized as 2D-center offset, log depth, log dimensions, 6D rotation; auxiliary heads for 2D detection (IoU-aware BCE, L1+GIoU) and depth/intrinsics estimation; one-to-many matching (k=4); ignore-region suppression for non-exhaustive 3D annotations.
2D sources: COCO, LVIS, Objects365, V3Det; MoGe-2 metric depth plus PerspectiveFields/WildCamera for pose and intrinsics.

Five candidate generators: 3D-MOOD, DetAny3D, SAM-3D, RANSAC-PCA, LabelAny3D, followed by translation/rotation optimization and rule-based geometric, depiction, composite-image, and LLM-estimated size filters.

Selection: Prolific crowdworkers (1,786 annotators, gold-task quality control) pick and rate the best candidate for ~103K images; a fine-tuned Molmo2 VLM scoring six criteria (keep score >10) auto-selects for ~896K images.
Totals: 1,003,886 images, 3.73M annotations, 13,499 categories (138x Omni3D), max depth 81 m; human-verified val/test splits form WildDet3D-Bench (700+ categories split into rare/common/frequent).

Three stages with AdamW (lr 1e-4), 32 GPUs, effective batch 128: (1) Omni3D 12 epochs; (2) Omni3D + WildDet3D-Data (human+synthetic) + CA-1M/Waymo/3EED/FoundationPose, 12 epochs; (3) Omni3D + human WildDet3D-Data with mask-guided point/box prompts, 3 epochs.
Per-prompt batching; each image-category yields one multi-target (text/exemplar) query and one single-target (box/point) query.

Benchmarks: WildDet3D-Bench (center-distance AP, LVIS-style federated protocol), Omni3D (3D-IoU AP over thresholds 0.05-0.50), zero-shot Argoverse 2 and ScanNet (ODS), and zero-shot Stereo4D with real stereo depth.
All settings evaluated in both text-prompt and oracle box-prompt modes, with and without depth input.
Baselines: Cube R-CNN, Uni-MODE, 3D-MOOD (Swin-T/B), OVMono3D-LIFT, DetAny3D.
Removing the 2D detection head (3D-only), the 3D confidence head, one-to-many matching, the auxiliary geometry loss, deep supervision, and ignore-aware suppression.

key_findings.finding: Training on the new WildDet3D-Data yields a step change in open-world 3D detection accuracy, especially on rare categories.
key_findings.evidence: On WildDet3D-Bench, text-prompt AP3D rises from 6.8 (Omni3D-only training) to 22.6 and box-prompt from 8.4 to 24.8, versus 2.3 for 3D-MOOD and 7.7/7.8 for OVMono3D-LIFT/DetAny3D; AP_rare reaches 28.3 (47.4 with depth) versus 2.4 for 3D-MOOD.

key_findings.finding: Making depth an optional, residually fused input lets one model exploit geometric cues at inference for very large gains without architectural change.
key_findings.evidence: WildDet3D-Bench AP goes 22.6->41.6 (text) and 24.8->47.2 (box) with GT depth; Omni3D 34.2->41.6 and 36.4->45.8 with sparse depth; zero-shot Stereo4D real stereo depth 7.5->27.7 AP (2.8x OVMono3D-LIFT's 9.9); ScanNet ODS 48.9->50.2 while Argoverse 2 is unchanged (40.3->40.4).

key_findings.finding: The unified promptable architecture sets a new state of the art on standard and zero-shot 3D benchmarks with an order of magnitude less training.
key_findings.evidence: Omni3D: 34.2 AP3D text (+5.8 over 3D-MOOD Swin-B) and 36.4 oracle (+2.0 over DetAny3D) using 12 epochs vs 80-120; zero-shot ODS 40.3 on Argoverse 2 and 48.9 on ScanNet (+16.5/+17.4 over 3D-MOOD Swin-B) with AP 43.4 vs 14.8 and 56.5 vs 28.8, plus the best mAOE (0.526/0.437).

key_findings.finding: Joint 2D+3D prediction in a shared head is the single most critical design choice for monocular 3D detection.
key_findings.evidence: Removing the 2D head collapses Omni3D oracle AP from 30.2 to 11.1 (SUNRGBD 33.9->5.1, Objectron 56.8->10.9); other components contribute smaller gains: O2M matching -2.5 AP, geometry loss -1.7 AP (concentrated indoors), 3D confidence head -0.8, deep supervision -0.3, ignore-aware suppression -0.2.

key_findings.finding: VLM scoring of candidate 3D boxes tracks human judgment well enough to serve as a pre-filter but cannot replace human verification.
key_findings.evidence: VLM composite score correlates perfectly monotonically with human rejection rate (Spearman rho = -1.0; 71.9% rejection below score 7 down to 9.2% at score 11), and its top-2 candidates cover 73.4% of human selections, yet 16.7% of score-10 candidates (64.5% of all candidates) are still rejected by humans; candidate-generator rejection rates vary over 3x (RANSAC-PCA 12.5% vs DetAny3D 42.9%).
